title: A pane hosts any app — Pane, content components, and the scene seam that makes Terminal a widget
summary: Integrate the shared API into pane/header ownership, managed lifecycle, input/floating parity, a second content and picker.
description:
Approved consolidation, 2026-10-25. This phase owns pane/content integration. The shared API foundation is P067/T517 -> T398, including native Terminal::new("shell"), public factory/binding semantics and the open registry. Do not rebuild it here. The full component contract is .planner/docs/p094-pane-hosts-any-app.md; accepted open-content decision 502849a5-af36-4331-8788-249dd6629c28 applies.

After completed T449 and shared T398, T450 moves the optional terminal header into content composition and removes the special PaneShell reservation, preserving Tag/actions/config/in-place refresh. T455 audits tree input acceptance already largely implemented and depends only on completed T451. T452 consumes T398/T450 for open managed creation/lifecycle/restore, without a second constructor/backend starter/registry. T453 audits the same managed content tiled/floating; T454 proves a second headerless component in panes and a dock. T457 converges the reusable picker, consuming the second-content proof and completed T432/T436.

Current main 6e3e6d36 already has T449's standalone retained Terminal, Label/Tag header fitting, shared tiled/floating PaneShell and tree-based raw pointer routing. Keep them. Terminal::new() remains internal and managed PaneEntry/gather remains Terminal-specific; those distinct gaps belong to T398 and T452. Do not implement the old hit-test/render paths again. Source sharing or deletion is not runtime acceptance.

T448/T449/T451/T456 stay done. Real multi-document tabs T550 and Requirement c4382108-0be4-4c1d-b112-871284c543cb moved to P106/F011. T550 retains its T452 task dependency; it does not wait for all P094 and no longer expands this phase's closure. T088 stays historically done; I009 is IDEA ONLY. Preserve T360/F012/P022 ownership.

Use Component/Parent/IntoChildren and ordinary one-or-many children/nested layouts, no closed content-kind enum or pane-only widget trait, no native factory/Box/cast ceremony. Plugin identity handles/typed descriptions retain their separate boundary. Canonical planner: /Users/antonio/projects/heca/.planner. Cold-start: verified P067 and P094 handoffs, then the chosen task/checklist. Planning changes start no implementation.

decisions: The scene seam is (a): enqueue_scene collects placements {id, rect, clip} and the host blits them in its own pass — single responsibility, the showcase needs no GPU pass, and wgpu types stay out of the crate boundary (Rule Zero).
The seam is generic — 'a component hosting content something else rasterises' — so image surfaces, video panes and a plugin's canvas get it for free. Not a terminal feature.
The terminal splits along the widget/component line: the surface-hosting widget in heca-grid-ui, Terminal itself in heca/src/components/terminal/ (mod.rs the only file touching AppState).
P097(F003) is a prerequisite of this phase, not an overlap. P097 owns the dispatch, P094 owns the terminal.
The previous handoff's 'PARKED on Antonio's instruction' was my own note quoted back as his decision. Disregarded.

The scene seam is: a widget records a request, the host performs the GPU work. Rejected giving the drawing pass an encoder and target — it would give a function that describes what to draw a second job (owning pass lifetime) and force every caller to supply one, including the showcase, which has no GPU pass of its own.

The seam is GENERIC — 'a component hosting content something else rasterises' — and serves two unrelated features: the terminal's texture and the frost's blur. Two features needing one seam is why it is the right shape rather than a convenience.

Collecting the requests is a PURE READ of the scene, so it is host_requests(scene) and not part of enqueue_scene. Discovered by trying the other way: it forced a signature change on every caller for something none of them wanted, and made the collection untestable because no test can build a renderer without a GPU.

The frost makes the seam a PREREQUISITE of moving layers into one tree, not a parallel task. The blur needs a moment where the scene holds everything beneath a surface and nothing of it; that moment exists today only because chrome and layers paint into two separate scenes, and disappears the instant they share one.
The terminal splits along the widget/component line: the surface-hosting widget in heca-grid-ui, Terminal itself in heca/src/components/terminal/.

T448's terminal half was RELOCATED to T449 by agreement with Antonio (2026-08-31). There is no pane-content widget tree to emit cx.surface from until the Terminal component exists, and bolting it onto the current direct-paint path (paint_terminal_pane_shell / blit_retained_terminal_layer) would be a throwaway T449 removes. HostDraw::Surface requests are a documented no-op in the render.rs host loop until then.

The frost half of the seam landed as Overlay::frosted(true) — a surface property, not a host pass — recorded in the scene's BASE band and performed by the host between the base flush and the overlay band. That is what stopped the frost breaking when P097/T494 collapsed chrome and layers into one scene.
The seam is generic and serves two unrelated features (the terminal's texture, the frost's blur), which is why it is the right shape rather than a convenience.

acceptedDecisions.title: Pane content is open component composition; no closed content-kind enum
acceptedDecisions.decision: Pane must accept arbitrary component content through ordinary child composition, including a collection of children or a nested layout tree. Terminal, Browser, Editor and future plugin-defined components are examples, not an exhaustive list. Do not introduce a closed PaneKind/content-kind enum or an exhaustive Terminal/Browser/Editor switch as the pane content dispatch mechanism. Content participates through a common component contract.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Antonio explicitly agreed 'no enum' and described the intended API as Pane::new(...).child([Comp1, Comp1]) or Pane::new(...).child(a layout containing components), with Terminal::new(), Browser::new() and arbitrary Other::new() usable as children. A new content implementation must not require editing Pane or Column.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Approved 2026-10-25 supersedes earlier exactly-one-child, closed PaneKind and Terminal-constructor-in-T452 wording. Reuse Component/Parent/IntoChildren with ordinary one-or-many/nested children; differing types may chain child calls. Direct native Terminal::new("shell") and standalone binding belong to P067/T398 after generic T517 templates. Plugin identity handles remain acceptable and sandbox code composes typed descriptions of host-exposed primitives, not native objects. T450 owns optional terminal headers; T452 consumes T398 for managed lifecycle/restore, never another constructor/registry. T453/T455 audit current float/input behavior, T454 proves a second content, T457 converges the picker. Real tabs T550 moved intact to P106, dependent on T452 only. T088 stays historical, I009 remains an IDEA, and T360/F012/P022 ownership is preserved. No implementation is started by this decision.

tasks.title: Step 1 — a component can host content something else rasterizes
tasks.description:
═══ PRE-FLIGHT (AGENTS.md § 0 — written 2026-08-19, before any code) ═══

1. WHICH EXISTING THING DOES THIS? The precedent is `Text`, exactly.
   - `DrawCommand` (heca-grid-ui/src/scene.rs, 631 lines) — six variants: Rect, Brackets, Text,
     Scanline, PushClip, PopClip. `TextCmd` (:379) is the model to copy: the scene names a **role**
     and the renderer resolves it ("which family that is lives here, so no widget knows a font's
     name" — heca-renderer/src/scene.rs:145). A surface command is the same bargain with a texture.
   - `enqueue_scene` (heca-renderer/src/scene.rs:92, 318 lines) is one `match cmd` with an arm per
     variant, over a clip stack that intersects nested `PushClip`s and scissors both renderers.
   - The blit already exists and must be REUSED, not rewritten: `blit_retained_terminal_layer`
     (heca/src/app/terminal_render.rs:292) draws `state.terminal_layers[pane_id]` through
     `state.backdrop.draw(..)` at `mount.content_rect`, scaled by `scale_factor`, with an optional
     stencil.

2. WHICH TASK COVERS IT? This one — P094(F011)/T448.

3. ⚠️ WHAT IS NEITHER — the design question this task must answer, found in the pre-flight:

   **`enqueue_scene` cannot do the blit.** Its signature is
   `(grid: &mut GridRenderer, text: &mut TextRenderer, scene: &Scene, glow_alpha_scale: f32)` — it
   feeds two renderers and has NO `wgpu::CommandEncoder` and no target view. The terminal blit needs
   both (`blit_retained_terminal_layer(state, pane_id, encoder, target, viewport_px, mount,
   stencil)`), and it happens in the GPU pass, not while the scene is being enqueued.

   So a new `DrawCommand` cannot be consumed the way the other five are, and there are two ways out:

   (a) **`enqueue_scene` COLLECTS them.** It returns (or fills) the surface placements it walked past
       — `{ id, rect, clip }` — and the host blits each one in its own pass, in scene order, with the
       clip already resolved. The library stays GPU-free and `enqueue_scene` keeps its signature's
       spirit: it still only turns a scene into draw work, and the caller owns the encoder.
   (b) **Give `enqueue_scene` the encoder and target.** Simpler to read at the call site, but it puts
       GPU-pass ownership inside a function that currently has none, and every caller (the app AND
       the showcase) has to supply them.

   (a) is the better fit and keeps the boundary the crate is built on, but it is a REAL choice about
   heca-renderer's shape — put it to Antonio before building, per § 0 rule 3.

   Ordering is the wrinkle either way: the terminal is drawn UNDER the pane chrome today (the shell
   paints after the terminal so the border is not swallowed). A collected placement has to keep that
   relationship rather than compositing on top.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

STEP 1 of P094. Everything from step 2 onward waits on this — but NOT step 0 (T451), which is the
pane shell and its letter and needs nothing from here. (T451 is DONE.)

THE GAP (verified 2026-08-18): heca-grid-ui/src/scene.rs `DrawCommand` has exactly six variants —
Rect, Brackets, Text, Scanline, PushClip, PopClip. There is NO `Custom` and NO `Gradient`, though
AGENTS.md's catalog line claims both. So a component has no way to say "my content is rasterized by
someone else; here is where it goes", which is why the terminal could never be a widget.

BUILD: one new DrawCommand variant naming an EXTERNALLY-RENDERED SURFACE — an opaque id plus the
rect it occupies. The library stays GPU-free: it emits an id and a rect and knows nothing else. This
is the same split `Text` already has — the scene says "this run of text goes here", heca-renderer
owns the atlas and decides how. docs/widgets.md states the principle for glyph glow: "The halo is a
renderer choice, not a scene one."

- heca-grid-ui: the variant + whatever `PaintCx` method emits it. Nothing about wgpu, textures or
  formats crosses into the library.
- heca-renderer: map the id to the texture it already holds and blit it at that rect, honouring the
  clip stack (PushClip/PopClip) so a surface inside a ScrollRegion clips like anything else.
- Who allocates the ids is the HOST's business, not the library's.

RULE ZERO: write the line a plugin author would type. A plugin that renders its own content into a
texture must be able to place it with one builder on its own widget — no host-private type, no
registry. If the answer needs either, the API is wrong.

ALSO IN THIS TASK: correct the stale AGENTS.md line that lists `Gradient` and `Custom` among the
DrawCommand variants, and document the new variant in docs/widgets.md (§ Scene / DrawCommand /
PaintCx) with both audiences, per the mandatory-docs rule.

VERIFICATION: a headless test asserting the command is emitted with the right rect and clip; the
visual proof comes with step 2.

**Completion summary:**
SHIPPED — the scene seam (a component can place content something else rasterises; a node can ask for a blur behind it).

Slice 1 (committed fd4a0b2): `DrawCommand::Host(HostCmd)` + `HostDraw::{Surface{id}, Backdrop{radius}}` in heca-grid-ui/src/scene.rs; `PaintCx::surface(rect,id)` and `PaintCx::backdrop_blur(rect,radius,alpha)` in heca-grid-ui/src/component.rs, with the scale arm (radius scales with a zooming subtree; id/alpha do not) and the fade arm (carries paint-context opacity). 5 tests in heca-grid-ui/tests/host_draw.rs. docs/widgets.md updated.

Slice 2 (committed 4d8d1bd): `heca_renderer::scene::host_requests(&Scene) -> Vec<HostRequest>` — a pure read of the display list, no GPU, each request carrying its clip already intersected with every enclosing PushClip and returned in scene order. 2 tests. `enqueue_scene` keeps its signature; the rejected alternative (hand it an encoder+target) is recorded in the phase decisions.

Slice 3 — the frost, on the seam (working tree, NOT yet committed; files heca/src/chrome/layers_glue.rs + heca/src/app/render.rs):
- paint_layers now records a `HostDraw::Backdrop` into the layer scene when any visible layer declared `LayerBackdrop::Frosted` — one full-viewport request for the whole frosted set, radius from theme `overlay_frost_radius`, alpha from `LayerRegistry::frost_opacity()` (the boldest frosted layer's own animated opacity). Its signature changed from `&AppState` to `&LayerRegistry` so it is testable headless.
- render.rs replaced the bespoke `wants_frost()` -> blur -> backdrop.draw block with a loop over `host_requests(&layer_scene)` that performs each Backdrop request (logical->physical via scale_factor, intersected with the recorded clip, then state.blur.process + state.backdrop.draw against the scene texture). Same GPU work, now driven by the scene in scene order.
- 2 headless tests in layers_glue.rs: a frosted layer records the request; a plain layer records nothing.

VERIFICATION:
- Headless: ./scripts/lint-changed.sh test green (664 + all other changed crates); ./scripts/lint-changed.sh clean apart from the two known pre-existing heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/toast/stack.rs:80 warnings.
- Visual: Antonio confirmed 2026-08-31 the exposé frost is pixel-identical. That was the intent — the frost was kept as one whole-frame request, so no visual change; per-layer-rect precision is deliberately left for T494 when each frosted layer is a real tree node emitting its own backdrop_blur with its own bounds.

RELOCATED, by agreement with Antonio 2026-08-31: the terminal blit switching to `cx.surface` is NOT done in this task. It belongs to T449, whose description already states the Terminal component "paints ONE command — the externally-rendered surface from step 1 — and nothing else". WHY THE SEAM COMES BEFORE T494: T494 moves layer roots into the one retained tree, which removes the accidental gap between the chrome scene and the layer scene where the frost blur is taken today. With the frost now a recorded request the host performs, that gap no longer needs to exist. T494 is unblocked.

DECISIONS:
- Frost is one full-viewport request for the whole frosted set — identical pixels to the previous hand-ordered pass. Two frosted layers up at once still share one pass.
- paint_layers takes &LayerRegistry, not &AppState (AGENTS 0b-bis rule 4).
- `wants_frost()` / `frost_opacity()` stay live (now consumed by paint_layers); `any_visible()` is now used only by its own registry tests but left in place — T494 reworks the registry.

tasks.title: Step 2 — Terminal becomes a component you can put anywhere
tasks.description:
STEP 2 of P094. Depends on step 1 (T448).

Antonio, 2026-08-18: "Terminal should be a reusable component similar to a DOM <terminal/> we can put
in any container in the app, even in a plugin or in a sidebar if we want."

TODAY: the terminal is not a component at all. heca/src/app/terminal_render.rs (1700 lines) renders
cells into retained GPU textures (sync_retained_terminal_layers, render_terminal_layer_update) and
blits them (blit_retained_terminal_layer), with stencil and scissor passes around it, plus
queue_terminal_dynamic_overlays. Its rect is computed by hand — stable_tiled_content_rect /
stable_floating_content_rect / pane_content_rect.

BUILD: heca/src/chrome/terminal/ per AGENTS.md § 0b-bis (mod.rs is the ONLY file that may touch
AppState; model.rs is the session reduced to plain data; testing.rs holds fixtures). The `Terminal`
component:
- is an ordinary Component: it gets bounds, focus, events, hit-testing, clipping and children from
  the framework like every other widget;
- paints ONE command — the externally-rendered surface from step 1 — and nothing else;
- takes its rect FROM THE LAYOUT ENGINE. Delete the hand-computed content rects: the engine gives
  the child its bounds, and the GPU pass reads them.

PRESERVE EXACTLY: retained terminal textures, damage tracking, the row-range merge, and the fact
that terminal cell glyphs carry no glow. Cell glyphs are the hottest path in the app. Drawing them as
ordinary scene commands is REJECTED and must not be attempted.

Also moves here: the per-pane viewport widgets (state.pane_viewport_widgets — the "N lines above"
BadgeButton and the scrollbar). They scroll the TERMINAL's scrollback, so they belong to the terminal,
not to the pane. Per the settled tree the terminal sits inside a ScrollRegion that the content owns.

CHECK: the pointer/keyboard funnel. Today mouse routing for pane content is hand-written in
heca/src/mouse.rs against pane rects; as a component it should receive events through the ordinary
tree dispatch. Run something before claiming either way.

VERIFICATION: Antonio drives. A terminal must look and behave identically — same text, same
selection, same scrollback, no new lag — and must additionally render correctly when mounted
somewhere that is not a pane.

---
**Completion summary:**

acceptedDecisions.title: Terminal: a component placed anywhere, a handle you keep, a session that outlives it
acceptedDecisions.decision: Lives in heca/src/chrome/terminal/ (mod.rs the only file touching AppState; model.rs; testing.rs). Placing it is one line: Terminal::new("shell") with builders for what runs (cwd, program, args, env) and how it looks (font_size). It has NO title and NO icon (those are the header's). Terminal::new(..) returns a handle; the handle and the terminal on screen are the same terminal, so changes through it show at once. program and cwd are fixed at start and do not change while running; to type into a running shell there is t.run("..."); t.kill() ends it. The shell is a session that lasts until killed or heca ends (with F012, until the server ends), so removing the terminal from a tree, or a rebuild, never kills it; a terminal with the same name shows the same session. The + / - font-size keys keep working per terminal: the component answers them itself when focused, the host wires nothing; .font_size(..) only sets the start size. cx.surface and the host loop are internals: nobody who places a terminal writes them. The pane border stays over the terminal because the pane frame draws around its content, never because the terminal knows about it.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Agreed with Antonio 2026-09-30. FIRST RULE: placing a component must not require the host to teach it anything, so a terminal starts its own session from its own attributes. A DOM-like element: place it anywhere, no container wiring.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Slices, each checked by Antonio by eye: (1) Terminal in the pane shell's content slot, host reads its laid-out bounds, delete stable_tiled/floating_content_rect, pane_content_rect and the header-inset arithmetic; (2) Terminal emits cx.surface, host performs the surface requests instead of the hand loop, tiled and floating, terminal still under the pane frame (study how the Pane paints frame vs children first); (3) the 'N lines above' badge and scrollbar move into the terminal inside a ScrollRegion; (4) selection, mouse reporting and scrolling become the component's own handlers and the hand-written pane routing in mouse/ goes. Before designing the live handle, check how other widgets take live values (signals). Renderer stays: retained textures, damage tracking, row-range merge, no glow on cell glyphs.

acceptedDecisions.title: Terminal process: store-issued id, one owner, run and kill are actions, size reported on change
acceptedDecisions.decision: The running shell behind a Terminal is called a TERMINAL PROCESS (TerminalId, TerminalSpec, the store's terminals API), never a "session": in F012 "session" already means an instance (P100). Identity is an opaque TerminalId handed out by the store on ensure; a name is only a property (shown, searchable, usable by RPC as a readable pick, resolved once at the edge). A pane's terminal gets its identity from the pane. The store (BackendStore) is the ONE owner of terminal processes, so P105 can save and restore them from it; a process lives until killed or heca ends and is never killed by rebuilding or removing the component. One door, ensure(spec), spawns; the six spawn sites (mutations.rs, startup.rs, handlers/split_resize.rs x2, handlers/system.rs, handlers/workspace.rs) collapse onto it inside T449, at the process slice, never before slices 1-2. ensure with a spec that differs from the running one keeps the running one and reports it once. run and kill are ACTIONS registered in the ActionCatalog (terminal.run with the text, terminal.kill, target = the terminal) and the handle's seam emits those intents through the normal path, so keys, the palette, RPC and heca-pro reach them with no second way in. The command seam comes from the build context (BuildCx), so Terminal::new("shell") stays one line. A Terminal writes its laid-out size into its handle in on_layout and the handle reports it only when it CHANGES (one resize message, which is what P104 sends), not a host read every frame. Needs no change in heca-core.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Architect review of the session design, 2026-09-30, on Antonio's delegation. A name used as the key is an id the caller has to get right (Rule Zero) and breaks on rename; P104 and P105 need a stable identity across windows and save/restore; run and kill as actions give heca-pro the one door it needs to send work into a terminal.

THE SHAPE THIS SHOULD TAKE, once the header moves (added 2026-09-16).

The pane's body is two parts — header and content — and today it is a Flex column holding
[header, content] with the host COUNTING THE CHILDREN to work out whether there is a header
(heca/src/chrome/pane/mod.rs::header_height: `match children.len() { 2 => ..., _ => 0.0 }`). That is
the pattern AGENTS § 0 and docs/layout.md both name as never right: put a second thing in the body
and the first is mistaken for a header.

WRITE IT AS A TEMPLATE. heca-grid-ui's Grid now speaks CSS, so the body is:

    Grid::new().template_row("auto 1fr").child([header, content])

The header takes its own height, the content takes the rest, a missing part is a missing row, and
nothing counts anything. A child that needs a particular place says so about itself — `.area("..")`,
`.column("1 / -1")`, `.row(2)` — because placement became the item's own property, as in CSS.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY: `header_height` exists only because the terminal is not a child of
the pane — it paints into the pane's rect, so something has to tell it how far down to start. Three
things read it: the terminal's content rect, the mouse→cell mapping, and the scrollback badge
position. When the header belongs to the terminal (this task) and the content is a real child, the
layout engine places them and `header_height` — and its child-counting — stop existing altogether.

See docs/layout.md for the full vocabulary, and P052(F004)/T350 for the share idiom (`.basis(0.0)`,
landed 2026-09-16).

1. WHICH EXISTING WIDGET / FUNCTION DOES THIS? Nothing here is new.
   - The frame: the grid-ui `Pane` widget through `chrome::apply_pane_frame` (chrome/theme.rs:147),
     which is exactly what paint_terminal_pane_shell already builds.
   - Retention: `chrome::sync_pane_headers` (chrome/pane_header.rs:952) is the pattern to COPY, not
     re-invent — phase 1 gathers per-pane inputs under immutable borrows, phase 2 builds only when a
     content key changed, then lays out, translates and prunes. With it: `RetainedPaneHeader { root,
     key }` (:280) and `pane_header_key` (:629), whose width BUCKETING (avail_w / 16.0) is what stops

   - The letter: `Base::hint` / `hint_style` / `HintPlacement::Center`, drawn by
     `component::paint_child`; collected by `heca_grid_ui::collect_hints`, handed out by
     `chrome::offer_hint_letters` (hint.rs:356), run by `fire_hint`, named by `target_identity`
     (:321) which already prefixes an identity with its surface.
   - The pick: `InteractionIntent::FocusPane { pane_id }` posted as `AppEvent::ChromeIntent` — the
     seam `PaneHeaderCtx.event_proxy` already uses for every header button. NOT `chrome::fires`
     (mod.rs:1344): that stamps a provider SEAT_ARG mount, and a pane is not seated in a chrome region.
   - The surface: `HintSurface::PaneHeader(PaneId)` (hint.rs:243) becomes the pane's.

2. WHICH PLANNER TASK COVERS IT? This one — P094(F011)/T451, absorbing the canceled P082(F003)/T447.

3. WHAT IS NEITHER — one thing, and it is a MOVE, not an invention:
   ⚠️ `pane_key(PaneId) -> String` ALREADY EXISTS TWICE, with two different strings:
     - heca/src/providers/workspaces/mod.rs:681 → "pane:7"          (the sidebar row)
     - heca/src/chrome/expose/pane_card.rs:19   → "expose.pane.7"   (the exposé card)

   the pane itself, and the pane must declare the SAME string — Antonio's rule: whoever owns the

tasks.title: Step 8 — one picker, not seven: a picker is a widget, and InputMode stops naming entities
tasks.description:
STEP 8 of P094. Decided with Antonio, 2026-08-18, from the question that exposed it: "I see hardcoded
InputMode. What if a plugin want to show and select some other entity? How do they do?"

They cannot. That is the defect.

═══ THE DEFECT ═══

`InputMode` (heca/src/app_state.rs) is a CLOSED ENUM IN THE CORE, and its pick variants NAME THE
ENTITY TYPE:

    InputMode::PaneSelect  { candidates: Vec<(char, PaneId)> }
    InputMode::PaneSwap    { candidates: Vec<(char, PaneId)>, focus_after: bool }
    InputMode::PaneTake    { candidates: Vec<(char, PaneId)>, focus_after: bool }
    InputMode::WorkspacePick { candidates: Vec<(char, usize)>, target: … }
    InputMode::ColumnPick  { candidates: Vec<(char, usize, usize)> }
    InputMode::FollowLink  { candidates: Vec<LinkHint> }
    InputMode::HintPick    { candidates: Vec<(char, HintTarget)> }

A plugin cannot add a variant, cannot build any of those candidate lists, and so cannot have the host
letter its containers, its files, its git hunks. **There is no line a plugin author could write.**
⭐⭐ RULE ZERO. No filter or argument fixes it — the shape is closed by construction.

Each variant also drags its own handler (handle_pane_select_mode, handle_pane_swap_mode,
handle_pane_take_mode, handle_follow_link_mode, handle_hint_pick_mode, + the workspace/column ones,
all in heca/src/app/input.rs), each re-implementing "match the typed letter, end the mode". Seven
copies of one rule — which is how the modifier guard came to be missing from four of them
(F011/P094/T451, 2026-08-18).

═══ THE ANSWER: A PICKER IS A WIDGET, AND IT ALREADY EXISTS ═══

    let open = signal(false);                 // flipped from an action
    KeyHintGroup::new(my_subtree).open_when(open)

That is the whole thing. The group holds focus while open — and holding focus IS taking the keyboard,
so there is no mode to enter, no gate to write and nothing the host must be told. It letters its own
descendants, claims the typed letter in the CAPTURE phase before the subtree sees it, and runs the
picked widget's own declaration. **The entity is never named in the core, because the picker letters
WIDGETS, not entities** — a plugin's Docker container is just a row that declared what picking it
does.

The exposé already works exactly this way and proves it: it declares `heca.expose.pick`, config binds
`[[keys.surface]] pick = "s"`, and `s` letters its cards only. There is no `InputMode::ExposePick`.

So `InputMode`'s pick variants are the LEGACY: they predate KeyHintGroup. The destination is that
every picker is a KeyHintGroup — a component's, a plugin's, and the core's, where `prefix+/` is that
widget at surface scope and `prefix+q` is the same with an eligibility filter.
docs/hint-architecture.md § 2c already says this in as many words.

═══ WHAT `prefix+q` VS `prefix+/` COSTS TODAY ═══
They are two implementations of one gesture, differing at every step:

| | prefix+/ (HintPick) | prefix+q (PaneSelect) |
| candidate is | a WIDGET (HintTarget{surface,path}) | a DOMAIN ID (PaneId) |
| targets found by | collect_hints, walking the laid-out tree | collect_all_pane_candidates, walking the SESSION |
| letter delivered by | offer_hint(root, &path, label) — BY PATH | offer_hint_by_key(root, key, label) — BY KEY STRING |
| what a pick does | fire_hint runs THE WIDGET'S declaration | the handler dispatches WmAction::FocusPane itself (input.rs:565) |

Row 3 is why the sidebar keycap is right-aligned under `prefix+/` and centred under `prefix+q`
(Antonio, driving, 2026-08-18): by-path lands on the widget that DECLARED the pick (the row's KeyHint
wrapper, carrying CenterRight); by-key lands on whatever node carries that key, with the default
placement. Same letter, two widgets, two looks. Neither placement is wrong.
Row 4 is why a plugin's pane could never join `prefix+q` however correctly it used the API: it is
never asked.

═══ WHAT TO BUILD ═══
1. `prefix+q` becomes the hint picker with an eligibility filter, not a mode. Its letters already come
   from the shared `assign_letters` (T451); this is the rest.
2. The picker's continuation is the caller's. Swap / take / move-to-column / move-to-workspace are
   "pick a target, THEN do X with it" — one picker that yields the chosen target, not five modes.
3. Delete: the InputMode pick variants and their handlers; collect_all_pane_candidates /
   collect_workspace_candidates / collect_column_candidates (heca/src/app/selection.rs);
   `offer_hint_by_key` + `offer_in_every_tree` + `wanted` (heca/src/chrome/hint.rs) — every target is
   then addressed the one way, by where it is in the tree, and the library stops having two doors for
   handing a widget its letter.
4. `InputMode::awaits_pick_letter` (app_state.rs:201) goes with them — the family it names stops
   existing.

═══ DEPENDENCIES — VERIFIED, AND NARROWER THAN FIRST CLAIMED ═══
- **T436 (P082/F003)** is the real prerequisite for the plugin half: KeyHintGroup has no `WidgetKind`
  and `on_action` has no declarative form, so a plugin can BE PICKED but cannot OWN A PICKER.
- **T432 (P082/F003)** is needed only for the GENERAL filter ("letter every target whose pick does
  X") and for dropping picks the policy would refuse — both need the pick to carry an `Intent`
  instead of an opaque `Box<dyn Fn()>`.
- **NEITHER is needed to fold `prefix+q` into the hint picker for panes**: a surface filter over the
  `HintSurface::Pane` added by T451 expresses "only panes" today, with no string parsing. Caveat: the
  sidebar row showing that pane lives in the Chrome surface, so a surface filter alone would not
  letter it — decide whether that is wanted before choosing.

═══ ALSO SETTLE HERE ═══
The pick's `InteractionSource`. T451 labels a pane pick `Keyboard` rather than `MouseContent`, on the
grounds that a pick carries no pointer (the same reasoning already applied to Rpc). It changes
behaviour in exactly one case — with a dock focused the domain becomes `Container`, so the pick is
allowed where `MouseContent` would resolve to `Floating` and refuse. NOT established by tracing: a
pick and a real click emitted the same source before that change, so no trace can separate them.

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
Antonio drives. `prefix+q` and `prefix+/` must be indistinguishable in look and placement, on panes
and on sidebar rows alike; swap/take must still work; and a second content kind (T454) must be
pickable by a picker it declares itself, with nothing added to the core.

Approved prerequisite map: consume T398's described/registry contract and T454's reusable second-content proof; T432/T436 are completed prerequisites, not new work. The implementation must reuse the existing KeyHintGroup/picker mechanisms.
